description: A 100-point shoulder assessment tool that combines patient-reported symptoms (pain and ADL - 35 points) with clinician-assessed measures (range of motion and strength - 65 points). Widely used in Europe for all shoulder conditions.
instructions: This assessment includes questions about your shoulder pain and function, followed by physical measurements that will be performed by your clinician.

total_score.calculation: Pain (15) + ADL (20) + Range of Motion (40) + Strength (25)
total_score.note: Age and gender-adjusted normative values available

sections.title: Subjective Assessment (Patient-Reported)
sections.description: Pain and Activities of Daily Living

questions.question: Activity level: What is the highest level you can use your arm without increasing your pain?

options.label: Full work - Work above shoulder level without restriction
Full work - Work at shoulder level
Able to wash and dress only

questions.question: Positioning: At what level can you get your hand behind your head with the elbow held back?

options.label: Yes - can get hand behind head with elbow back

questions.question: Positioning: Can you place your hand behind your back to the waist level?
Positioning: Can you place your hand behind your back to reach the lower thoracic vertebrae (bottom of shoulder blades)?

options.label: Yes - hand to lower thoracic spine

questions.question: Positioning: Can you place your hand behind your back to reach the interscapular region (between shoulder blades)?
Positioning: Can you place your hand behind your back to reach the neck of the 12th dorsal vertebra (top of shoulder blade level)?

sections.title: Objective Assessment (Clinician-Measured)
sections.description: Range of Motion and Strength - To be completed by clinician

questions.question: Range of Motion: Total active forward elevation in degrees (0-180°). Award 1 point per 10 degrees up to 150°, then 1 point per 5 degrees from 150-180°.
questions.calculation_note: 0-30° = 0-3 pts, 31-60° = 4-6 pts, 61-90° = 7-9 pts, 91-120° = 10-12 pts, 121-150° = 13-15 pts, 151-170° = 16-19 pts, 171-180° = 20 pts. Then add lateral elevation, external rotation, internal rotation scores (clinician calculated).

note: Full scoring includes clinician-measured components: Range of Motion (40 points) includes forward elevation, lateral elevation, external rotation, and internal rotation. Strength (25 points) measured with dynamometer or manual resistance. Patient completes questions 1-7 only.
